blockers.title: The claimed census-derived do-not-record and history prose remains stale, so mandatory predecessor findings are falsely marked LANDED.
blockers.claimAttacked: findingDisposition says CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1 landed because doesNot is generated from the census and names every unrecorded frozen version; authorityClaim introduces its recital as the lineage's own history.
evidence: The thirteen predecessor objects report no COORD recording for v1, v2, v3, v4, v6, v9, v11, v12, and v13. Those are the nine frozen, unrecorded predecessors measured by the subject's own census.
doesNot[13] names only v7, v9, and v8. Of the nine unrecorded predecessors, it names only v9 and omits v1, v2, v3, v4, v6, v11, v12, and v13.

CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1 occurs twice in findingDisposition, at indexes 42 and 63, with identical LANDED text claiming that the enumeration is generated from the census and names every unrecorded frozen version rather than three. The bytes still contain the same three-version sentence.

authorityClaim says 'Its own history is this' and then begins at v5. It omits v1 through v4 even though basedOn and predecessorStanding now correctly census them, so the authorityClaim limb of PPBSV13-B1's required repair remains incomplete.
The prompt expressly attacks both a disposition that claims a landing the bytes do not show and a do-not-record enumeration that omits an unrecorded frozen version.
blockers.impact: The application-grade provenance contains a directly false mandatory-finding landing claim and presents a hand-stale boundary as census output.
requiredRepair: Generate the authority history and the do-not-record enumeration from the same measured predecessor census used for basedOn.
At minimum enumerate v1, v2, v3, v4, v6, v9, v11, v12, and v13 as frozen and unrecorded, while separately distinguishing the recorded historical versions v5, v7, v8, and current recorded v10.
Do not mark CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1 or the authorityClaim limb of PPBSV13-B1 LANDED until those generated bytes actually appear.

blockers.title: basedOn.relation retains the exact broad no-other-change claim its mandatory landing entry says was replaced.
blockers.claimAttacked: findingDisposition says PPBSV13-B4 landed because basedOn.relation carries the held-constant and added statement 'in place of' the broad claim attacked by CLAUDE-PPBS-V12-ADV-4.
evidence: basedOn.relation still says the subject refreshes four citations and two partitions 'and changes nothing else'. This is the exact broad clause PPBSV13-B4 required replacing.

The very next sentence says v14 also adds the measured D-316 standing, a census-generated predecessor record, and a recomputed doesNot union. Appending an additions inventory does not put it in place of the retained broad clause.
PPBSV13-B4 occurs twice in findingDisposition, at indexes 49 and 70, with identical LANDED text saying the broad claim was replaced. CLAUDE-PPBS-V12-ADV-4 is also marked LANDED on the same premise.
The normalized class equality and stable-payload comparisons do pass, but they support a scoped payload-constancy statement, not the retained whole-artifact wording.
blockers.impact: A mandatory v13 finding and the earlier finding it carries forward are not landed, and their disposition text contradicts the named field.
requiredRepair: Delete the broad 'changes nothing else' clause from basedOn.relation.
State separately the enumerated additions and the exact stable payload fields proved equal to v10, keeping normalized class equality scoped to the fourteen class payloads.
Re-evaluate PPBSV13-B4 and CLAUDE-PPBS-V12-ADV-4 against the repaired bytes before marking them LANDED.

shouldFix.title: findingDisposition duplicates all thirteen v13 finding objects.
shouldFix.finding: The array has 74 rows but only 61 unique identifiers: 59 unique reviewer findings plus two internal NOTE identifiers. Each of the thirteen v13 identifiers occurs twice, and each repeated object is byte-for-byte equal to its first occurrence. Set closure passes, but this is not a one-record-per-finding disposition registry and makes later count and mutation checks ambiguous.
shouldFix.repair: Emit each of the 59 reviewer finding dispositions exactly once, retain the two distinct internal NOTE rows, and assert both identifier-set closure and identifier uniqueness.

shouldFix.title: The narrowed carried-standing NOTE still includes a disposition that was not carried from v10.
shouldFix.finding: The NOTE defines the dispositions carried from v10 as those sourced from Stage A reviews of v2 through v9. CLAUDE-PPBS-V2-ADV-1 is sourced from the v2 review, but it is absent from v10's findingDisposition and is newly restored in v14 as one of the eight identifiers v13 omitted. The revised scope therefore still falsely describes at least that row as carried from v10, so PPBSV13-S1 is not fully landed.
shouldFix.repair: Scope the NOTE to an explicit set of identifiers actually present in v10, or say that it covers only v10's carried disposition rows and excludes newly restored census entries.

shouldFix.title: A mandatory landing disposition gives the wrong predecessor-object count for v13.
shouldFix.finding: The disposition says all thirteen predecessors are now pinned 'not the six preview-product-boundary-successor.v13 carried'. Frozen v13 contains eight predecessor objects, predecessorV5 through predecessorV12. The numeric comparison is false and triggers the prompt's number/word-agreement attack.
shouldFix.repair: Replace 'six' with 'eight' after regenerating the disposition from the measured predecessor-key count.
